title: Public feedback on the proposed 2026 budget
subtitle: Delegations on immigration funding, Pitch Kitchener, business retention, downtown events and the corporate climate action plan.
overview: The Finance and Corporate Services Committee held a special meeting to hear public feedback on the proposed 2026 Budget. The minutes record no motions and no recommendations, so nothing was decided at this meeting. Five delegations spoke, and the committee asked questions.

The Waterloo Region Immigration Partnership Council asked the City for $25,000 in funding after a substantial cut in federal support. Staff suggested Council consider the request when the draft Newcomer Strategy is presented, and staff plan to recommend that the City consider partnerships with organizations doing immigration work.

Delegates from Communitech, the Waterloo Economic Development Corporation and the Downtown Kitchener BIA supported budget items for Pitch Kitchener, the Business Retention and Expansion program and the Special Events Strategy. One resident questioned the budget for the Corporate Climate Action Plan 2.0 and asked how it would be paid for. Staff said it is meant to draw on savings from completed projects and possible provincial and federal programs.
Residents should watch for how these points are handled when the budget comes back for decisions.
debate: The immigration delegate said federal funding was cut and the partnership has a funding gap. It asked each local government for support, and said newcomers will keep arriving whatever the national totals. The delegate also said senior governments hold much of the responsibility.

Committee members asked how the request fits with the City's Newcomer Strategy. Staff said the strategy's themes overlap with the partnership's work, and that funding could be aligned with its objectives once the draft comes to Council.

Communitech presented Pitch Kitchener as a model for local procurement of homegrown technology. It said participating companies valued both the revenue and staff feedback. Councillors asked about extending the model to advanced manufacturing and other municipalities.

The economic development delegate backed business retention and suggested roundtables for local subsidiaries of international companies, a pilot to move technology firms from co-working to office space, and continued work with senior governments. Councillors asked about downtown vacancy and defence and trade opportunities.

A resident argued that climate action plans are voluntary and asked where funding for the plan would come from. Staff said the full annual amount in the plan has not been allocated. They pointed to an energy revolving fund fed by project savings such as LED streetlights, net-zero new facilities, and possible grants.
